## RULING 254 — show everything we find, and say one thing about it

*`R-0254` · ACTIVE · author_explicit · 2026-09-03 · also cited as `RULING 254`, `R254`, `R-254`*

- **supersedes_full** → `R-0023`
- **supersedes_full** → `R-0026`
- **supersedes_full** → `R-0027`
- **supersedes_full** → `R-0028`
- **supersedes_full** → `R-0042`
- **supersedes_full** → `R-0044`
- **supersedes_full** → `R-0047`
- **supersedes_full** → `R-0050`
- **supersedes_full** → `R-0051`
- **supersedes_full** → `R-0059`
- **supersedes_full** → `R-0105`
- **supersedes_full** → `R-0138`
- **supersedes_full** → `R-0139`
- **supersedes_full** → `R-0149`
- **supersedes_full** → `R-C-non-negotiables-in-code-the-deferral-boundary-falls-between-subj`

**Everything the product holds renders. Collection state never governs display. There is no threshold, no completeness bar, and no circumstance under which a candidate, a contest, a body, a meeting or a field is suppressed because something else is missing. A gap in one field has no bearing on any other field, candidate or contest. Completeness is a property of the hunt; the answer to an incomplete hunt is more hunting.**

- **No COLLECTION-COMPLETENESS suppression path may exist in the codebase** — nothing may hide a candidate, contest, body, meeting or field because the hunt is incomplete or because something else is missing, whether live, flagged, disabled or commented out, and a guard test fails the build if one returns. This is not a bar on identity, provenance, legal, safety, neutrality or unresolved-contradiction controls, which may hold only the smallest affected fact, its inseparable comparison pair, or the single record — never unrelated verified truth: an unreviewed image renders nothing while its card renders in full. The hunt-state field is the disambiguator and never reaches a reader — `NOT_APPLICABLE` renders nothing, `NOT_HUNTED` renders its named gap, `VERIFIED_ABSENT` renders a source-backed field-specific fact, `FOUND` renders the value — and it is a work queue, never a gate.
- **An absent field renders nothing.** No row, no placeholder, no dash, no "still looking." Cards in a contest may be different lengths and that is correct. The only disclosure is one asterisk on the contest heading and a footnote beneath the cards.
- **The page says one thing about completeness and nothing else:** *"What we have found, we are displaying here."* Once in the ballot section, once on the battlecard. No other sentence anywhere describes coverage, counts what is missing, or characterises what has not been worked out — not per card, not per page, not on the about page. A coverage claim goes stale the moment the work behind it is done; a named gap does not.
- **A null renders as its named gap, and the name says whose gap it is.** "We haven't recorded this yet" is a fact about us; "not in this chamber for this vote" is a fact about them. They never render as the same sentence. **The product never announces its own failure:** state what is known, offer the narrowing, move on. The attribution is required; a verdict on ourselves is struck.
- **Stated N equals rendered rows, everywhere, always.** Where collection and rendering can diverge, three numbers are reported: rendering, deliberately out of scope and why, and in scope and still dark.
- **Photos-first ordering is presentation; withholding data is suppression.** The two are unrelated. Sources collapse to one line at the bottom of a card; the record beneath is never deleted.
- **The coverage matrix is generated, internal, and never rendered to a reader in any form.**
- A named gap renders in the gap's own visual register, never in a present value's styling — colour and style are claims too, so an absence may not wear a recorded value's appearance.

## RULING 255 — neutrality is symmetric effort, explained absence, and nothing invented

*`R-0255` · ACTIVE · author_explicit · 2026-09-03 · also cited as `RULING 255`, `R255`, `R-255`*

- **supersedes_full** → `R-0055`
- **supersedes_full** → `R-0112`
- **supersedes_full** → `R-0118`
- **supersedes_full** → `R-0126`
- **supersedes_full** → `R-0143`
- **supersedes_full** → `R-0167`
- **supersedes_full** → `R-0171`

**Equal effort per candidate and per side of every contest. Asymmetric output is legitimate only when source truth differs; different investigative effort because one candidate was easier to research is a system defect. The neutrality audit compares matched candidates and contests mechanically, unexplained asymmetry blocks promotion, and the gate is always on and not operator-disableable.**

- **Equal effort lives in the hunt.** A hunt session works a contest as a unit — every candidate in it — before moving on, rather than filling the incumbent because the incumbent is easy. The Kelly standard is the definition of done per candidate — photo, phone, working contact, specific verified page, campaign site — with no tiers; a candidate meets it in full or carries an argued absence per field, and there is no partial credit.
- **Rendering symmetry.** An incumbent has years of votes and filings; a challenger has a campaign site. When a record class is absent for one candidate, the reader is told what is absent and why ("no voting record — has not held this office"; "no reports on file with [authority] as of [date]"), and no surface may let record volume read as merit.
- **The questionnaire is symmetric by construction, or it is not shipped.** Identical questions, word limits, deadline, reminders, and rendering of non-response. Answers publish verbatim and are never summarized. It is the only instrument that closes an asymmetry that lives in the source material.
- **Never generate a candidate position.** Every position, vote or stance carries a source record pointing at a specific statement, roll-call, filing or questionnaire response; if none exists, the field is null. Never infer from party, endorsement or similar candidates. LLM summaries paraphrase a cited source and never fill a gap. Every blurb carries its source class.
- **The product never tells anyone how to vote.** No ranking, recommended ballot, match, fit, alignment or compatibility score, and no ordering by anything but a neutral criterion. A reader asking directly is not an exception.
- **A ballot measure is done at seven fields, no tiers:** official text and summary cited; plain-language decoding; household cost in units a person feels (cite the official estimate or say `NO_OFFICIAL_ESTIMATE` with where we looked — never estimate it ourselves); who certified it; money for; money against; sources. Equal effort for and against is constitutional: both sides ship at equal depth or neither ships, and the check refuses rather than reports. `NONE_REGISTERED` is legal only on money fields with the filing officer named and is never interchangeable with `NOT_HUNTED`.
- **Campaign finance renders for readers and never enters anything sold.** Donor rendering is aggregate only — totals, source types, in-state versus out, employer rollups; no individual donor name or address renders anywhere, for federal or state data. Absence of filings renders as "no reports on file with [authority] as of [date]," never as $0. Organizations render as filed, never characterized.
- **An appointed official never carries the govern verb** ("runs the department," "chair"). **A photo ships through one of four doors** — explicit licence, official government portrait, campaign self-published portrait, last-resort .gov or campaign site — and only an author-reviewed image renders; a review decision is about an image, never about a person, and a pending photo never withholds the card. Photo review is tracked one row per session listing the N photos decided, never one row per photo — a per-photo row would flood the queue with dozens of rows a session.
- Social-media images are never a portrait source at any of the four photo doors — a candidate's self-published social image does not become a usable portrait, and a compliant route that fills the campaign-site field is not thereby a photo door.

## RULING 256 — scope, identity, and what fills a field

*`R-0256` · ACTIVE · author_explicit · 2026-09-03 · also cited as `RULING 256`, `R256`, `R-256`*

- **supersedes_full** → `R-0054`
- **supersedes_full** → `R-0064`
- **supersedes_full** → `R-0065`
- **supersedes_full** → `R-0071`
- **supersedes_full** → `R-0074`
- **supersedes_full** → `R-0121`
- **supersedes_full** → `R-0122`
- **supersedes_full** → `R-0145`
- **supersedes_full** → `R-0222`
- **sets** `rendering.address_scope` = `address-scope-replaces-zip-scope`
- **sets** `rendering.excluded_entity_label` = `prohibited-out-of-scope-not-annotated`

**Before a confirmed address the scope is the ZIP: every governing entity intersecting it renders. After a confirmed address the scope is the address: only entities that govern it render. Show-everything guarantees completeness within the correct scope; it never licenses displaying an entity that does not govern the reader, and a "not yours" label is prohibited — out of scope is not annotated.**

- A ZIP cannot answer "who governs you"; a street address can. Once given, an address persists for the session and resolves every surface that could use it; it is never asked for twice.
- A body that governs territory in more than one town is one body with one identity, listed in every town it covers.
- A candidate's filed mailing address renders — it is public information. A contact that reaches an office rather than a person is published, labelled as the office. The site footer is a named branch and is walked before an address is recorded absent.
- A page on a party's site or an official presence on a platform, reached by a compliant route and carrying the candidate's name, office, own words and a contact, fills the campaign-site field with the host labelled. Facebook only by compliant routes — ad library, archive, mirror, news embed — never authenticated access.
- After an address narrows scope, an overlapping body whose governance of the reader has been determined to be nothing — neither confirmed nor excluded — stays exactly as it was; dropping it manufactures a false claim that it does not govern the reader.

## RULING 257 — a fix is proved on the reader's path, against a case it did not come from

*`R-0257` · ACTIVE · author_explicit · 2026-09-03 · also cited as `RULING 257`, `R257`, `R-257`*

- **supersedes_full** → `R-0025`
- **supersedes_full** → `R-0114`
- **supersedes_full** → `R-0133`
- **supersedes_full** → `R-0134`
- **related_to** → `R-0147`
- **supersedes_full** → `R-0153`
- **related_to** → `R-0157`

**A verification states the reader's route to the thing it verifies and walks it. A test that exercises only the code path the fix introduced has proved that the code does what the code does. The verification must also exercise at least one case the fix was not derived from, named in the report.**

- No reconciliation compares a parser to itself; every reconciliation names its external anchor.
- A layer that always renders is asserted against a source of record, and a mismatch fails rather than renders.
- A performance change ships with its before-and-after measurement; an instrument without a committed baseline is unfinished.
- Reader-facing behaviour is never degraded to fix an internal problem.

## RULING 258 — reader surfaces speak plain language

*`R-0258` · ACTIVE · author_explicit · 2026-09-03 · also cited as `RULING 258`, `R258`, `R-258`*

- **supersedes_full** → `R-0140`

**No OCD-ID, no enum value, no `NO_SOURCE_FOUND`, no hunt-queue vocabulary reaches a reader. Dates spell out — full month, ordinal day, four-digit year — through one formatter, product-wide. The register is chosen by surface; the stranger test is that a person who has never heard of this product understands the sentence on first read. Reader friction is a defect, with exactly three exceptions: the transparency disclosure at reaction capture, the optionality of the narrowing prompt, and anything constituting consent to collection.**
